newsitem.title: UK: Ivorian cocoa weather looking more optimistic-WSC.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa weather looking more optimistic-WSC.

text.p: Light showers forecast in Ivory Coast cocoa areas later this week suggest a more optimistic outlook for the midcrop, an agricultural meteorologist said on Tuesday.

"They did get some scattered thunderstorms late in February... and there is some risk of a few afternoon showers, especially towards the end of this week. So that's a little bit optimistic," said Joel Burgio of Weather Services Corp, contacted by telephone.
"Maybe we will move to spring and pick up some better (rain) activity," he said.
Ivory Coast often has a dry, hot month ahead of the rainy season, and this did not necessarily imply that the rains would be late or less than normal, Burgio said.
It appeared to him that February's unusually dry conditions, which put stress on cocoa trees, were unlikely to continue in March after an increase in moisture levels recently.
The midcrop totalled as much as 200,000 tonnes last season.
Its sizer this year will determine whether the Ivorian crop is in line with government estimates of less than one million tonnes, or nearer to last year's record of 1.2 million.
Burgio said that for a healthy midcrop, a below normal-type rainfall pattern needed to continue well into April.
"They need the rain to develop and be consistent," he said.
"If we get a big rain surge early and it quits us that's probably more harmful than if it were just delayed," he added.
But as in other tropical areas which don't lend themselves well to long-range weather outlook, forecasting more than just a few days in advance was very difficult, Burgio said.
